summary: On 6 February 1934, French far-right leagues stirred up by an antisemitic press and the Stavisky fraud scandal tried to storm the Chamber of Deputies in Paris; police fire left many dead and the government fell.

evidence.note: story opens with the Dreyfus affair as the root of the French far right
Dreyfus pardoned 1903, cleared 1906; affair fuels antisemitic radical press
long segment on mass-circulation right-wing papers driving outrage
1924 Cartel victory and left-centre coalition politics through 1932
Maurras profile: monarchist, Dreyfusard, founder of Action Francaise
Croix-de-Feu under La Rocque: veteran league with mass vote control
Stavisky's pawn-shop bond fraud described at length
Stavisky's death spurs murder and cover-up conspiracy theories
6 February 1934 march on the Chamber, police open fire
short epilogue: February 6 veterans in Vichy, Maurras jailed 1945

notes: Transcript dates the Dreyfus arrest to 1884; it was 1894, used here. Vichy and Maurras's 1945 sentence get only about three minutes, so covered_span ends in 1934. January 6 2021 parallels are comparisons only. Guest is Jason Petty, known as Prop. No polity id for the French Third Republic.
